title: pm(dispatch-gates): derive a gate family for the governed file its self-test reads
body:
Fixes #18673

Clause-②: no

`maskSelfTests` blanks every self-test body before `extractWatchHints` runs, and that mask is right for the reason its own docblock measures — a self-test is made of fixture paths, and admitting them printed a gate in the MATCHED column for most of the tree. But a self-test case can also assert a STRUCTURAL fact about a real tracked file: `scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs` asserts that the enqueue bar in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` still names it. That read is not a fixture, it is a population claim on a file a card edits, and the mask dropped it with the fixtures. What it cost is on the record: a PR re-keying that bar derived its gate list with this tool, ran every derived family to exit 0, reconciled with `--ran` at 0 NOT-MEASURED, and `Lint & Repo Gates` went red on `check:pm-expected-skips` — the family the list did not contain. A reconciliation's zero is a statement about the DERIVED set, so a family outside that set is invisible to it by construction: a list that confirms itself is more dangerous than no list.

## The derived list, before and after

Change set: `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` alone. Measured twice each way — once with the path fed on argv and once from a throwaway commit in a scratch worktree, `--changed` semantics; both derive the same set, because both reach `derive(paths, …)` by the same call.

| | derived commands | `pnpm check:pm-expected-skips` | `--ran` over the 18-line run record |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (`f8eaf6704`) | 18 | absent | `18 derived, 18 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` — the false green |
| after (`26dc4f5369`) | 19 | present | `1 of 19 derived famil(ies) UNRUN — pnpm check:pm-expected-skips [absent from the run record]` |

The row now reads:

```
- pnpm check:pm-expected-skips   [lint.yml]   matched via .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md
  ⇢ declared self-test read by scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs '.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md'
```

With all 19 run, the reconciliation closes again: `19 derived, 19 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. `--ran` is unchanged in meaning; it now reconciles a set that contains the family.

## The mechanism — one declaration, one spelling

```
// dispatch-gates: self-test-reads PATH [PATH ...] -- REASON
#  dispatch-gates: self-test-reads PATH [PATH ...] -- REASON      (shell gates)
```

- **Why a declaration rather than a widening.** `anchoredReadTargets` already resolves this read — it scans unmasked source, so the self-test's `readFileSync(join(ROOT, '.claude/…/SKILL.md'))` comes back from it today. What drops it is `readProgramTargetsInSource`'s boundary: a followed read must be PROGRAM TEXT, because a gate that parses a data file it found by walking a tree would otherwise contribute every fixture it ever touched. Dropping that boundary re-admits the class the mask exists to refuse. A declaration is decidable where a widening is a guess, and it puts the fact on the file it describes.
- **ADMITTING only, never INVENTING.** Every declared path is checked against `anchoredReadTargets` of the same source text and REFUSES (throws) on a path that is not there. The declaration can only re-admit a read the scan already sees and the boundary dropped. A declaration whose read is DELETED stops parsing and reddens every run of the tool — which is what makes the pin below unsatisfiable by deleting the read.
- **One spelling, deliberately.** The two path-list markers (`inherited-population` and this one) are now built from one `MARKER_LINE_HEAD`, so the indent, comment form and key are spelled ONCE for both; a self-test case pins that the two patterns differ only in their key. Written as a `//` whole line with the reason on that same line, so it parses under today's grammar and survives both queued marker cards behind this one (#18661, comment forms; #18662, the reason-cut reading) whichever way they land.
- **The read edge carries a label.** Discovery records `declared-self-test` in a new `entry.readEdge` map beside `entry.readOrigin` (the counterpart of `hintEdge`), and `coveringKey` prints `declared self-test read by FILE` rather than `program text read` — a dev reading the row has to know which claim to go check.

## The class, not the instance — the census pin

`governedReadCensus()` scans every tracked `scripts/**` JS/TS source for an anchored read of a GOVERNED surface (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`) and reports each `(script, file)` pair with whether the script declares it. Its eyes are deliberately WIDER than the derivation's follow: it scans with `GOVERNED_READ_CALL`, a strict superset adding the asynchronous and `promises` spellings, so a governed read the follow cannot carry is REPORTED rather than silently absent. `GOVERNED_READ_FLOOR` pins the population; four self-test cases hold the tree to it, and the fourth is the deliverable stated over the whole class: **every governed file a script structurally reads is DERIVED for the family that runs that script**, however it is spelled.

The measured census on this tree is three rows:

| script | governed file | declared | derived today, via |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs` | `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` | no | `gate source` |
| `scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs` | `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` | **yes** | `declared self-test read` |
| `scripts/pm/check-settings-deny-roster.mjs` | `.claude/settings.json` | no | `gate source` |

The two undeclared rows are the named list this PR does NOT declare: both already spell their governed path in their MODULE BODY as well as in their self-test, so `extractWatchHints` sees it and the derivation already names the family for a card touching that file — measured, both ways, at this landing. They cost nothing today, and declaring them would widen this PR onto two gates it was not dispatched to. They are a floor the next card lowers, and the roster reds in every direction that matters: a read that disappears, a new governed read, and a `declared` flag that moves either way.

## Ablation, from the committed fix

Blob-verified at `HEAD:scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs` = on-disk `775cc9f4`, the declaration line deleted on disk (marker grep 1 to 0, blob `ed526a71` — the mutation is proven landed, not inferred from an editor exit code), then:

- derivation for the SKILL.md change set: back to **18** commands, `check:pm-expected-skips` absent;
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test`: **5 of 1788 cases fail**, and only these five —
  - `check:pm-expected-skips is derived for the SKILL.md its self-test reads (no key)`
  - `every governed read in the census is DERIVED for the file it reads` — reading: `check:pm-expected-skips`, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, verdict `silent`
  - `each pinned row's DECLARED flag still reads off the file (pinned declared=true, live declared=false)`
  - `the census is not vacuous — it finds the declared row AND undeclared ones`
  - `…and the 0 DECLARED data read(s) are the only hole in it, each one really carried (none)`

Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- FILE`: on-disk blob back to `775cc9f4`, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty. The restore is proven by blob identity and an empty diff, never by an exit code.

## Self-test readings, at `26dc4f5369`

Reconciled: `dispatch-gates --ran: 30 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 30 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) at `26dc4f5369`: exit 0, no output. Not a narrowed run — the whole repository, so no narrowing has to be argued.

`skip-changeset`: the diff is two files under `scripts/pm/`, which no package's `files[]` publishes; nothing released moves.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope and noted, not filed: #18661 and #18662 are queued on this same file behind this card. This declaration's spelling was chosen to survive both — a `//` whole line with a one-line reason — and the shared `MARKER_LINE_HEAD` means #18661's comment-form widening lands in one place for all five markers rather than two.
